nodes.label: Authority ID (glossary term: the random value that names one journal; the configuration repeats it as the authority witness, so a missing journal is not taken for a first start)
Bootstrap (glossary term: the explicit operator command that creates a journal once, from the expected writer and matching fresh observations of every node; the daemon never does this by itself)
Journal (glossary term: the SQLite file that holds the approved topology and quarantine and, later, operations and audit events; one daemon owns one journal)
Restore hold (glossary term: the mark a journal carries when it came out of a backup; admission stays closed until an operator reconciles it)
Identity ID (glossary term: the name an operator gives one entry of the identity map; logs and metrics use it in place of the principal or the backend login)
Conflict latch (glossary term: the durable mark a cluster gets when a second primary or a later timeline was observed; writes stay closed until an operation clears it, also when the evidence is gone)
Baseline File (text list of what a workspace guard allows today)
Branch Rule (GitHub ruleset for main kept as a repository file; avoid branch protection)
Core MVP, Routing preview, V1 (release gates, not version numbers)
Expected writer (glossary term: the node the configuration names as the writer of a cluster; it seeds the approved writer at bootstrap and must keep agreeing with it)
Fresh Model (session that did not write or design a change)
Required Check (named PR check; same name in scripts/check.sh, CI job and branch rule)
Node (glossary term: one configured PostgreSQL server of a cluster, with a stable ID, a host and a port; a backend is a connection to a node)

Authority revision (glossary term: the durable counter that rises with every change of the approved topology, the quarantine, a membership decision or the restore hold; a mutation of durable authority names the revision it expects)
Start sequence (glossary term: the durable counter that rises by one each time the daemon opens its journal to serve; a generation that lives in memory is only comparable inside one start sequence)
Principal (glossary term: one frontend identity that may log in, as an entry of the configuration with a name and a verifier; before authentication succeeds, the name a client sends is only a claim)
Principal ID (glossary term: the name an operator gives one principal entry; logs use it in place of the principal name)
Verifier (glossary term: what POOL holds to check a frontend password with SCRAM, in the form PostgreSQL stores; it is not a password and cannot be used to log in to PostgreSQL)
Monitor login (glossary term: the PostgreSQL role the probe logs in as; it has the right to log in and nothing else)
Handshake permit (glossary term: the bounded right of one connection to be in startup and authentication; its limit is separate from the session permits)
Backend permit (glossary term: the bounded right of one session to hold a backend on one node; a session waits for it in a bounded line)
Route view (glossary term: what the data plane reads to find the eligible primary of a cluster: the topology snapshot, mapped by the daemon into a type that the data plane owns)
Probe (glossary term: the task that asks one node for its role, system identifier and timeline and produces observations)
State directory (glossary term: the directory named by control.state_directory; it holds the journal and the lock file, and its owner is the service account)
